## Discovery & Translational Science

- **[Big Pharma]** **Novartis gene therapy Zolgensma linked to pediatric tumor risks** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/06/novartis-zolgensma-gene-therapy-tumor-risk/) / [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/zolgensma-tumor-report-novartis-sma-spinal-muscular-atrophy/873990/)
  - Disclosed nine total cases (including seven previously unreported) of tumors arising in pediatric spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) patients treated with adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy Zolgensma (onasemnogene abeparvovec).
  - Genomic analysis confirmed viral vector integration into host genomic DNA in at least two cases, heightening safety concerns regarding AAV integration-site mutagenesis across gene therapy platforms.

- **In vivo CRISPR base editing of ANGPTL3 achieves durable lipid lowering** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42994815/)
  - In vivo base editing targeting *ANGPTL3* demonstrated persistent reduction of circulating triglyceride and lipid levels in animal models.
  - Results support single-dose base editing as a potential therapeutic approach for severe dyslipidemia.

- **Circulating tumor DNA detects subclinical cancer in systemic sclerosis and dermatomyositis** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26364657)
  - Prospective tracking of 134 adults with recent-onset systemic sclerosis (SSc) or dermatomyositis (DM) identified circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) in 4 of 6 patients who subsequently developed clinically diagnosed malignancies.
  - Plasma ctDNA positivity preceded clinical cancer detection by a median of 13 months (range 1.4–17), showing identical somatic mutations between cell-free DNA and matched primary tumor tissue.

- **Serum IGF-1 levels correlate with attenuated functional decline in ALS** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26366903)
  - Longitudinal evaluation across 48 inter-visit intervals in 37 amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) patients revealed that each 1-SD higher serum IGF-1 level at a prior visit predicted a 1.40-point lesser subsequent decline on the ALSFRS-R functional scale.
  - Findings suggest systemic IGF-1 serves as a circulating trophic-metabolic marker of functional reserve in ALS.

- **Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies healthy donor kidney aging signature reflected in diabetic kidney disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367347)
  - Profiling 24 healthy living donor biopsies (aged 36–66) using a 5,101-gene spatial transcriptomics panel revealed age-dependent loss of cellular contact between immune cells and tubular epithelium.
  - Applying the living-donor tissue-aging score to 28 diabetic kidney disease (DKD) biopsies independently predicted post-biopsy eGFR decline, with aging scores successfully predicted directly from routine periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) histology slides.

- **Clonal hematopoiesis linked to elevated risk of lung adenocarcinoma and esophageal carcinoma** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367360)
  - Prospective UK Biobank cohort analysis linked clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) to incident solid tumors overall (HR 1.13, 95% CI: 1.08–1.19).
  - Histologic subtype analysis revealed statistically significant associations specifically for lung adenocarcinoma (HR 1.79) and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (HR 2.28), with risk escalating alongside clone size and multi-hit mutations.

- **Histone deacetylase inhibitor Trichostatin A rescues disuse muscle atrophy** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.30.763257)
  - In a 14-day murine hindlimb suspension model, systemic administration of Trichostatin A (TSA) restored disrupted Lamin A/C organization and H3K9me3 heterochromatin foci.
  - HDAC inhibition significantly attenuated the upregulation of atrophy-related gene expression networks and prevented loss of locomotor activity.

- **Satellite cell glucocorticoid receptor restrains myogenic commitment** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.04.764308)
  - Conditional deletion of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR) in satellite cells reduced PAX7⁺ stem cell counts during muscle regeneration in young mice without compromising net tissue repair.
  - GR silencing in human myoblasts induced early myogenic differentiation markers (including *MYOG*) without altering proliferation, demonstrating a conserved role for GR in maintaining stem cell quiescence.

## Early Trials — Phase I–II

- **Path to Prevention platform trial targets prodromal Neuronal α-Synuclein Disease** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.04.26367306) / [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.04.26367309)
  - Details the design of the Path to Prevention (P2P) Phase 2A platform trial embedded within the observational Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative (PPMI).
  - Utilizes a two-stage adaptive randomization scheme (n=125 per active arm) to evaluate biologically targeted therapies in non-manifesting or prodromal Neuronal α-Synuclein Disease (NSD) prior to clinical Parkinson's disease diagnosis.

- **MDMA-assisted psychotherapy demonstrates efficacy in social anxiety disorder** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42994762/)
  - A randomized, open-label, wait-list controlled Phase 2 trial confirmed clinical improvements in social anxiety symptoms following MDMA-assisted therapy.

- **Audio-visual gamma stimulation enhances neural coupling in cognitive impairment** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.06.26367319)
  - An 8-week randomized feasibility trial in 38 older adults with cognitive impairment evaluated self-selected music paired with 39-Hz gamma light stimulation versus non-gamma control.
  - Treatment strengthened theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, which correlated with significant cognitive gains on face-name association testing and ADAS-Cog scores.

- **Plant-derived extracellular vesicles combined with growth factors demonstrate scalp and hair efficacy** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.07.26362401)
  - A 56-day randomized placebo-controlled trial (n=60) evaluated a topical formulation combining *Centella asiatica* and ginger extracellular vesicles with recombinant long-acting IGF-1 and FGF-7.
  - The combination regimen achieved a 67% reduction in excess scalp sebum by Day 56 alongside superior hair density and growth kinetics compared to placebo and mono-components.

## Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

- **[Big Pharma] Add-on GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy substantially reduces cardiovascular events and mortality in ASCVD** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.05.26367396)
  - A real-world propensity score-matched study (119,911 matched pairs) evaluated GLP-1 receptor agonists added to baseline statin therapy in patients with established ASCVD and BMI ≥30 kg/m².
  - Over 3 years of follow-up, add-on GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a marked reduction in all-cause mortality (4.0% vs 7.5%; HR 0.479, 95% CI: 0.463–0.496, p < 0.001), myocardial infarction (HR 0.762, p < 0.001), and ischemic stroke (HR 0.671, p < 0.001).

- **Pooled trial analysis characterizes sudden cardiac death risk in HFmrEF and HFpEF** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42994786/)
  - Individual patient-level pooled analysis across five major Phase 3 randomized trials defined clinical predictors and incidence of sudden death in patients with heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.

## Regulatory & Approvals

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves subcutaneous amivantamab formulation (Rybrevant Faspro) across all indications** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-amivantamab-and-hyaluronidase-lpuj-subcutaneous-injection)
  - Approved amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj for subcutaneous injection covering all existing adult indications of intravenous amivantamab in EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
  - Approval based on the Phase 3 PALOMA-3 trial demonstrating non-inferior pharmacokinetics and comparable efficacy between subcutaneous amivantamab plus lazertinib and intravenous amivantamab plus lazertinib.

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves belantamab mafodotin (Blenrep) combinations for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-belantamab-mafodotin-blmf-relapsed-or-refractory-multiple-myeloma)
  - Approved BCMA-targeted antibody-drug conjugate belantamab mafodotin with bortezomib and dexamethasone for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma following at least two prior lines of therapy.
  - Efficacy supported by significant progression-free survival improvements in the Phase 3 DREAMM-7 trial.

- **[Big Pharma] FDA grants traditional approval to acalabrutinib (Calquence) plus BR in frontline mantle cell lymphoma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-acalabrutinib-bendamustine-and-rituximab-previously-untreated-mantle-cell-lymphoma)
  - Approved BTK inhibitor acalabrutinib in combination with bendamustine and rituximab for transplant-ineligible, previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) based on the Phase 3 ECHO trial (n=598).
  - Converted single-agent acalabrutinib from accelerated to traditional approval for adults with relapsed or refractory MCL.

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves gemcitabine intravesical system (Inlexzo) for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-gemcitabine-intravesical-system-non-muscle-invasive-bladder-cancer)
  - Approved a drug-releasing intravesical system delivering gemcitabine over extended periods for adults with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with carcinoma in situ.
  - Supported by complete response data from Cohort 2 of the single-arm Phase 2 SunRISe-1 trial (n=83).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves fixed-dose niraparib and abiraterone (Akeega) for BRCA2-mutated mCSPC** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-niraparib-and-abiraterone-acetate-plus-prednisone-brca2-mutated-metastatic-castration)
  - Approved dual-action tablet niraparib and abiraterone acetate with prednisone for adults with deleterious or suspected deleterious *BRCA2*-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.
  - Efficacy validated by investigator-assessed radiographic progression-free survival in the randomized Phase 3 AMPLITUDE trial (n=696).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves inavolisib (Itovebi) triplet for PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- breast cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-inavolisib-palbociclib-and-fulvestrant-endocrine-resistant-pik3ca-mutated-hr-positive)
  - Approved PI3Kα inhibitor inavolisib in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant for endocrine-resistant, *PIK3CA*-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
  - Efficacy established in the double-blind Phase 3 INAVO120 trial (n=325) alongside companion diagnostic approval for the FoundationOne Liquid CDx assay.

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves first-line lazertinib plus amivantamab (Lazcluze/Rybrevant) for EGFR-mutated NSCLC** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-lazertinib-amivantamab-vmjw-non-small-lung-cancer)
  - Approved oral third-generation EGFR TKI lazertinib in combination with EGFR/MET bispecific antibody amivantamab for first-line treatment of EGFR exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution-positive advanced NSCLC.
  - Efficacy demonstrated in the active-controlled Phase 3 MARIPOSA trial (n=1,074).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA expands isatuximab (Sarclisa) to frontline transplant-ineligible multiple myeloma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-isatuximab-irfc-bortezomib-lenalidomide-and-dexamethasone-newly-diagnosed-multiple)
  - Approved CD38-directed monoclonal antibody isatuximab with bortezomib, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone (Isa-VRd) for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients ineligible for autologous stem cell transplant.
  - Supported by progression-free survival benefits in the Phase 3 IMROZ trial (n=446).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves durvalumab (Imfinzi) for limited-stage small cell lung cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-durvalumab-limited-stage-small-cell-lung-cancer)
  - Approved anti-PD-L1 antibody durvalumab for adults with limited-stage small cell lung cancer (LS-SCLC) whose disease has not progressed following concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy.
  - Supported by overall survival and progression-free survival improvements in the Phase 3 ADRIATIC trial (n=730).

- **[Biotech] FDA approves cosibelimab (Unloxcyt) for advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-cosibelimab-ipdl-metastatic-or-locally-advanced-cutaneous-squamous-cell-carcinoma)
  - Approved anti-PD-L1 antibody cosibelimab-ipdl for adults with metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma who are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation based on Study CK-301-101 (n=109).

- **[Biotech] FDA approves axatilimab (Niktimvo) for refractory chronic graft-versus-host disease** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-axatilimab-csfr-chronic-graft-versus-host-disease)
  - Approved CSF-1R blocking antibody axatilimab-csfr for chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) after failure of at least two prior lines of systemic therapy based on overall response rates in AGAVE-201 (n=241).

- **[Biotech] FDA expands liposomal irinotecan (Onivyde) into frontline metastatic pancreatic cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-irinotecan-liposome-first-line-treatment-metastatic-pancreatic-adenocarcinoma)
  - Approved irinotecan liposome plus oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin (NALIRIFOX) for first-line treatment of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma based on Phase 3 NAPOLI 3 trial results (n=770).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA grants full approval to erdafitinib (Balversa) for FGFR3-altered urothelial carcinoma** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-erdafitinib-locally-advanced-or-metastatic-urothelial-carcinoma)
  - Converted accelerated approval to full approval for FGFR kinase inhibitor erdafitinib in post-systemic therapy *FGFR3*-altered locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma based on Phase 3 BLC3001 Cohort 1 (n=266).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA expands radiopharmaceutical lutetium Lu 177 dotatate (Lutathera) to pediatric GEP-NETs** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-lutetium-lu-177-dotatate-pediatric-patients-12-years-and-older-gep-nets)
  - Approved SSTR-targeted radiopharmaceutical lutetium Lu 177 dotatate for pediatric patients 12 years and older with SSTR-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors based on pharmacokinetic and safety data from NETTER-P.

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves pediatric indication for inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa)** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-inotuzumab-ozogamicin-pediatric-patients-acute-lymphoblastic-leukemia)
  - Approved CD22-directed antibody-drug conjugate inotuzumab ozogamicin for pediatric patients aged 1 year and older with relapsed or refractory CD22-positive B-cell precursor ALL based on complete remission rates in a 53-patient pediatric study.

- **[Biotech] FDA approves first-line ALK inhibitor ensartinib (Ensacove)** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-ensartinib-alk-positive-locally-advanced-or-metastatic-non-small-cell-lung-cancer)
  - Approved ALK inhibitor ensartinib for adult patients with ALK-positive locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC without prior ALK inhibitor exposure based on PFS superiority over crizotinib in eXALT3 (n=290).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA expands alectinib (Alecensa) to adjuvant ALK-positive NSCLC** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-alectinib-adjuvant-treatment-alk-positive-non-small-cell-lung-cancer)
  - Approved ALK inhibitor alectinib for adjuvant treatment following complete surgical resection in ALK-positive NSCLC based on Phase 3 ALINA trial (n=257).

- **[Big Pharma] FDA approves subcutaneous atezolizumab (Tecentriq Hybreza)** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/cancer-approvals/fda-approves-atezolizumab-and-hyaluronidase-tqjs-subcutaneous-injection)
  - Approved co-formulated subcutaneous atezolizumab and hyaluronidase-tqjs across all adult indications of intravenous atezolizumab based on IMscin001 trial.

## Business & Strategy

- **[Biotech] / [Big Pharma] Stradbio acquires dropped Seagen ADC assets from Pfizer** [@JacobPlieth](https://x.com/JacobPlieth/status/2118765326162677950)
  - Newly launched Stradbio, headed by Seagen's former chief medical officer, acquired rights to two Seagen-originated antibody-drug conjugates that Pfizer discontinued following its acquisition of Seagen.

- **Decision quality frameworks in biopharma portfolio management** [Nature Reviews Drug Discovery](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41573-026-00173-8)
  - Strategic review detailing decision quality architecture and methodologies for evaluating asset viability during portfolio renewal cycles.

## Public Health & Policy

- **Global extinction of Influenza B/Yamagata linked to pandemic contact reductions** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.22.26358639)
  - Global epidemiological modeling indicates that the apparent global extinction of the influenza B/Yamagata lineage following 2020 was primarily driven by its lower basic reproduction number ($R_0$) relative to B/Victoria during COVID-19 population-level contact reductions.

- **States mount legal challenge against federal Medicaid work requirements** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/06/states-sue-trump-delay-medicaid-work-requirements/)
  - A coalition of U.S. states filed a lawsuit to block executive implementation of Medicaid work requirements, alleging immediate coverage disruption and irreparable harm to state healthcare systems.

- **Resignation of executive health advisor highlights internal dispute over industry influence** [STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/06/calley-means-joe-rogan-trump-maha-agenda-derailed-by-corporate-influence/)
  - Resigned MAHA administration leader Calley Means publicly stated that federal health policy priorities were compromised by corporate influence.

- Biology & Health
    - [Incredible Berberine Discovery](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/AFSZH4112no) -- Physionic
        - Research indicates metformin and berberine lower blood sugar in part by mildly inhibiting intestinal cell mitochondria, causing the small intestine to act as a metabolic sink that burns glucose for energy.
        - Human clinical data in type 2 diabetes patients demonstrated that metformin treatment approximately doubled glucose uptake by the small intestine.
        - Mechanistic experiments showed that preventing mitochondrial inhibition in intestinal cells eliminated berberine's glucose-lowering effect.
        - The findings demonstrate that blood sugar regulation involves turning the intestine into a major consumer of glucose, expanding understanding beyond liver-centered mechanisms.
    - [The difference between psychological and mechanical limits in lifting | Jeff Cavaliere](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Kst46m2gyLA) -- Peter Attia MD
        - The podcast episode addresses the concept of junk volume in strength training and how to differentiate productive reps from wasted effort.
        - Guest Jeff Cavaliere discusses managing workouts with a partially torn labrum and rotator cuff, noting that complete rest can impede recovery.
        - The discussion highlights the importance of targeting underemphasized muscle groups, including calves, glutes, and smaller stabilizing muscles.
        - Indicators requiring midlife training modifications are identified, including persistent joint soreness, elevated fatigue, and irritability.
- Pure Science
    - [Physics Has a Time Problem](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/31EvD6sSWYM) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Physicist Carlo Rovelli posits that time is not fundamental, as modern physics equations have gradually replaced time with change and entropy.
        - The video highlights Rovelli's thermal time hypothesis, which suggests that the perception of the flow of time originates from the physics of heat.
        - It examines how the physical evolution of the universe connects directly to the human experience of past and future.
- Tech & Engineering
    - [Why There Are So Many Different Hotel Brands](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fz9vY4DVCQ8) -- Wendover Productions
        - The transcript consists of promotional links and sponsorship details for Ridge tech gear.
        - It provides social media handles, email contacts, and platform links for Wendover Productions.
        - Detailed production credits attribute writing to Sam Denby, editing to Alexander Williard, alongside credits for animation, design, sound, and thumbnail creation.
